items.gist: Above the purest covering, the single Śaiva city is the mokṣa covering; eleven Rudras are established there.
Above the dhruva covering is the ichchhā covering with Śivas; above that, the prabuddha covering is marked by eight directional Rudras.
The great samayā covering contains five worlds and Sadāśiva; his Śakti performs the five cosmic acts.
The passage enumerates Rudras, mantras, and related Śiva forms within the Sadāśiva enclosure.
The Suśiva covering is surrounded by Rudras, Śaktis, and parivāra; its Rudras are omniscient and Śiva-formed.
Above the bindu covering is the Śāntyatīta Śiva with Śakti; the nivṛtti kalās and laya tattva are described.
Bhoga is taught in the bindu covering, while subtle bodies are not separately visible due to extreme subtlety.
Five nirodhikā kalās are named; piercing them leads to the supreme Sadākhya world.
Above the bindu is the great nāda enclosure with a lotus, directional worlds, and surrounding Śaktis.
The suṣumnā nāḍī, supported by nāda, pierces the universe and carries ascending and descending Śaktis.
The brahmabila covering contains Brahmā and Parā Devī, who grants liberation.
The Śakti tattva is described with vyāpīśa and the unattached Anāśrita Śiva.
Samanā is the cause of causes; māyā stands below as karma-form, while the unattached Lord directs the five causes.
Nāda, bindu, and related principles are the created effect; all up to Sadāśiva is called prākṛta.
The text gives bhuvana counts, nivṛtti, and differing views on purification and Rudra numbers.
Bhuvanas are enumerated by water, fire, air, space, ego, intellect, and guṇa tattvas.
The passage concludes with tattva counts, pāśa, and sixteen bhuvanas in the puruṣa.
